resources.string: Forces pen digitizer mode and 60/120 Hz refresh rate when detached without waiting for Bluetooth handshake, enabling third-party pens.
Select display refresh rate for stylus mode

When the stylus is in use (detached from the magnetic charger), the display automatically caps to 60/120 Hz to support stylus input. When the stylus is magnetically docked to charge or disconnected, the full 144 Hz refresh rate is automatically restored.

Smart cover open and close behavior
This toggles the behavior of the smart lid

Enable this only if you own the Xiaomi Smart Keyboard. When enabled, the system will (hopefully) automatically detect keyboard connection and manage power states. Disabling this saves battery and system resources.\n\nNote: This is separate from Bluetooth keyboards, which work without this setting.
Suspend battery input to run directly from the charger
Status: Active — Battery input is suspended
Bypass charging is not supported by the current kernel
When enabled, power flows directly from the charger to the device, bypassing the battery. The battery will not charge while this is active.\n\nThe feature resets automatically on reboot.
Set the maximum refresh rate for a specific application
Control the saturation level of the display
Changing the color mode in display settings will override the saturation level, requiring it to be reapplied.
Boost CPU scheduling for the active app
Not supported by the current kernel
may increase background app kill rate

Raises the CPU scheduling priority of the app currently on screen and, at higher levels, the foreground app stack.

Off — no boost applied (system default).
Low — mild boost to the top app only.
Medium — moderate boost to both the top app and foreground apps.
High — strong boost. At this level the kernel may reclaim memory from background apps sooner, which can cause apps to reload when you switch back to them.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Controls how the CPU scales its frequency
Not supported by the current kernel

Smart (schedutil) — Scales CPU frequency based on actual scheduler load. Best balance of performance and battery for everyday use.

Performance — Locks all CPU cores to maximum frequency at all times. Most consistent performance but drains battery faster and runs hotter. Recommended for sustained gaming.

Power Save — Locks all cores to minimum frequency. Reduces battery drain significantly but makes the device feel sluggish. Only useful for very light tasks.

Note: The governor may be temporarily overridden by the system during app launches or touch events. This is normal.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Limit the maximum speed of the main CPU core
Not supported by the current kernel

Limits the maximum clock speed of the PRIME CPU core (cpu7). Only the top core is capped — LITTLE and BIG cores are unaffected.

Useful for reducing device temperature and battery drain during long gaming or video sessions where peak performance is not needed.

Warning: Setting this too low will cause noticeable performance drops in demanding apps and games. If the device feels sluggish, raise the cap or remove it entirely.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Controls how the Adreno GPU scales its frequency
Not supported by the current kernel

Smart (msm-adreno-tz) — Qualcomm's thermal-aware GPU governor. Scales GPU frequency intelligently based on load and temperature. Best for everyday use and gaming.

Performance — Locks the GPU at maximum frequency (670 MHz) at all times. Delivers the most consistent frame rates but increases heat and battery drain. Best for demanding games where stable GPU performance matters more than temperature.

Power Save — Locks the GPU at minimum frequency (305 MHz). Drastically reduces battery drain but makes any GPU-heavy tasks feel slow. Only suitable for simple 2D tasks.

On Demand — A generic frequency scaling governor. Ramps GPU frequency up quickly on load but without the thermal awareness of msm-adreno-tz.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Limit the maximum clock speed of the Adreno GPU
Not supported by the current kernel

Limits the maximum clock speed of the Adreno GPU. Useful for reducing heat and stabilising frame rates during long gaming sessions — a capped GPU running consistently at a lower frequency often feels smoother than one that throttles unpredictably under thermal pressure.

Tip for gaming: Try 490 MHz or 525 MHz for a good balance of stable frame rates and manageable temperatures.

Warning: Setting this too low will cause visible frame drops and stuttering in GPU-heavy games and apps. If graphics feel slow or choppy, raise the cap.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Push tasks toward larger CPU cores
Not supported by the current kernel

When enabled, the kernel scheduler actively pushes tasks toward the larger BIG and PRIME CPU cores instead of letting them run on the LITTLE cores.

This improves sustained performance and reduces the chance of the active app feeling sluggish, but increases power draw since the larger cores consume more energy.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Controls how eagerly tasks move between CPU clusters
Not supported by the current kernel

Conservative — Tasks stay on LITTLE cores longer. Saves battery but may feel slightly slower during bursts.

Default — Balanced thresholds. Good for everyday use.

Aggressive — Tasks move to BIG and PRIME cores more readily. Improves responsiveness and reduces micro-stutters but increases battery drain, especially from background apps.

Warning: Aggressive migration may increase background battery drain noticeably.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
How quickly the CPU responds to sudden load spikes
Not supported by the current kernel

Battery — Lower hispeed targets. The CPU ramps up more slowly and conserves power. May feel slightly sluggish during short bursts like opening apps.

Default — Balanced hispeed settings. Works well for general use.

Responsive — Higher hispeed targets and a slower downscale rate. The CPU ramps up faster and stays elevated longer after a spike. Reduces stutter during fast interactions and gaming at the cost of slightly more power usage.

Only takes effect when CPU Governor is set to Smart (schedutil).

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Briefly boost CPU speed on screen touches
Not supported by the current kernel

When enabled, the CPU briefly ramps up to a higher frequency whenever the screen is touched. This makes taps, swipes and scrolling feel snappier by ensuring the CPU is ready to handle input immediately.

The boost lasts for the duration set in Boost Duration, then the CPU returns to normal scaling.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Shift tasks to larger cores during touch events
Not supported by the current kernel

When enabled, the scheduler also migrates running tasks toward the BIG and PRIME CPU cores during touch events, on top of any frequency boost.

Works best when combined with Touch Boost. Improves touch responsiveness in apps that have work queued up at the moment you interact with the screen.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
How long the CPU stays boosted after a touch
Not supported by the current kernel

Controls how many milliseconds the CPU stays at boosted frequency after a touch event.

Short (40ms) — Minimal boost. Saves battery but may not cover the full response cycle for heavier apps.

Normal (80ms) — A lighter option that still covers most UI interactions.

Default (120ms) — The kernel default. Covers the full UI response cycle for most apps.

Long (200ms) — Extended boost. Useful for apps with slow frame rendering, but increases battery drain noticeably with frequent touch input.

This setting only takes effect when Touch Boost is enabled.

Reapplied automatically after reboot.
Restore all Performance and Touch settings to their default values
All Performance and Touch & Input settings will be restored to defaults. Accessories, Display and Battery settings are not affected.
